fields.name: Śrīkṛṣṇa Sārvabhauma
fields.place: Navadvīpa (court of Rāmakṛṣṇa, Rāmajīvana and Raghurāma); of the Vārendra clan
fields.notes: Of the Sānyāl family (Vārendra), in the line of Rāmakṛṣṇa Vidyāvāgīśa; scholar-poet of the Navadvīpa kings Rāmakṛṣṇa, Rāmajīvana and Raghurāma (land grant 1703, given to his disciple Rāmajīvana Pañcānana in 1706). Wrote the Padāṅka-dūta and Kṛṣṇa-padāmṛta, and Nyāya works praising Kṛṣṇa.

fields.name: Viśvāsa (secretary of the Muslim governor)
fields.place: The Orissa border, on Lord Caitanya's way to Vṛndāvana
fields.notes: Secretary of the Muslim governor beyond the Orissa border; sent to the Orissa officer when Lord Caitanya was waiting there on His way to Vṛndāvana, he saw the Lord and began to chant «Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa» in ecstatic love. (The record's text breaks off here.)

Zamindār of Bhāturiyā, head of revenue under Āzam Shāh of Gauḍa and the power behind his successors; in 1407, guided by Narasiṁha Nāḍiyāl (Advaita's grandfather, #986), had Sultan Śamsuddīn removed and became king of Gauḍa. Padmanābha (ancestor of Rūpa and Sanātana) and Narasiṁha were at his court; Kṛttivāsa was honoured there.
